chapter_note: Despite lacunae and a brief compilation-style transition (¶5) plus a minimal episodic opener (¶1), the chapter is overwhelmingly systematic cosmogonic narration in Manichaean cosmological idiom (Darkness/Death, five dark elements, abyss/storehouses, Father of Greatness, First Man, five garments/sons). No NT citations or pastoral/institutional grafts appear; no seam flags are present.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Episodic bridge opener (“Once again it happened…as I have told you”) functions as a redactional/hagiographic reset rather than impersonal exposition; too fragmentary to recover an underlying core statement.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Programmatic cosmological limitation (no prior revealer) followed by a temporal marker (“from the time when it stirred…against the light”) launching the war narrative; impersonal explanatory style is core.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.70⟩
[The Fi]rst Man came forth against it and prevented it, [he kept] it apart from the house of the living. He prevented it. From that time, when the light was mixed with [the] darkness, and life [wi]th death, there was a measure of approval and an ability for [the] first-born [and the a]postle[s] to teach about it. They speak and unveil how the reproach and the fight did hap[pen], [how] the light [was] entwined with the darkness, which they [ ... ] life in death.
paragraphs.removed_material: Nothing removable with confidence: the paragraph fuses core war/mixture narration with compilation-era mediation language (“apostle[s]”) that marks the teaching as something later authorities ‘teach about’. Because ‘apostle’ is a Layer-2 marker but embedded in the only surviving sentence, the whole paragraph cannot be cleanly separated.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core content (First Man preventing intrusion; mixture of light/darkness, life/death) is old; however, ‘apostle[s]’ and the metadiscursive claim about who is permitted to teach about it suggest later compilation framing interwoven into the line.
